svg.title: workstation-steward: a checkout brought level after merges
svg.desc: An illustrative session, looping, in three scenes. After PR #12 and a Renovate PR merge on GitHub, steward fleet sync plans a fast-forward of two commits and drops one local edit that upstream already has. With --apply it asks, fast-forwards and writes a receipt; git log shows both merges. steward fleet prune-merged --apply finds the local branch fix/readme, whose PR merged and whose remote is gone, keeps main, asks, deletes it and records its tip in a receipt.

text.tspan: # PR #12 and Renovate's #13 just merged on GitHub
[3/4] comparing local edits with upstream: 1 overlapping path(s), 0 other local edit(s) stay (0s)
main: 2 commit(s) to fast-forward to origin/main
plan only. Add --apply to do it (asks first, backs up what it drops).
Drop the edits above and fast-forward? [y/N]
To restore a dropped edit, copy it back from its backup. (total 1s)
[1/3] reading the checkout: acme/web: 2 local branch(es) (0s)
[2/3] checking each branch against GitHub: 1 to delete (1s)
fix/readme (PR #12 merged, remote gone, nothing newer)
To bring one back: git branch <name> <tip> (tips are in the receipt). (total 1s)
